components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The optional honorific title of the pet owner, one of MR, MRS, MS or
            DR. When present it is combined with the last name to compose the owner's
            salutation. Stored and returned when supplied.
          type: string
          example: DR
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner. Accepted on input for backward
            compatibility, and always returned as the composed, normalized address. When the
            structured fields are supplied the returned value is the normalized addressLine1,
            with a single space and the normalized addressLine2 appended when addressLine2 is
            present. Optional on input as long as a non-blank addressLine1 is supplied instead.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine1:
          title: Address line 1
          description: The first line of the pet owner's structured postal address. Preferred
            over the flat 'address' when present. Normalized like 'address' (upper-cased,
            whitespace collapsed, common street-type abbreviations expanded). A non-blank value
            satisfies the owner's address requirement in place of the flat 'address'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '10 King St'
        addressLine2:
          title: Address line 2
          description: The optional second line of the pet owner's structured postal address
            (for example a unit or apartment). Normalized like 'address' when present and, when
            present, appended to the composed 'address' after a single space.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'Unit 4'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner. The value is normalized to
            E.164 form. Spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped. A leading '+' and country
            code are kept when present, otherwise country code '+61' is assumed and a single
            leading '0' is dropped from the national digits. The result must be a '+'
            followed by 8 to 15 digits. For example '0412 345 678' is stored as '+61412345678'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[-0-9()+.\s]*$'
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. When present it must be a
            syntactically valid address; it is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: The owner's 4-digit postcode. Optional. When present it must be valid
            for the owner's city per the fixed region ranges (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099,
            QLD 4000-4099); a city with no known region accepts any 4-digit postcode. Stored
            and returned when supplied.
          type: string
          pattern: '^[0-9]{4}$'
          example: '2000'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the pet owner was registered. When omitted on create it
            defaults to the server's current date. Returned in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date

## Summary

I implemented the `ownerSegment` derived field on the Owner API response.

**Changes:**

1. **`src/main/resources/openapi.yml`** — Added the `ownerSegment` property to the `Owner` schema as a read-only string enum (`PREMIUM_METRO`, `PREMIUM_REGIONAL`, `STANDARD_METRO`, `STANDARD_REGIONAL`), so the generated `OwnerDto` carries the field and its `OwnerSegmentEnum`.

2. **`src/main/java/.../mapper/OwnerMapper.java`** — Added a `@Mapping` for `ownerSegment` and an `ownerSegment(Owner)` method that composes `<TIER>_<AREA>`:
   - **TIER**: `PREMIUM` when the owner's derived `getMembershipLevel()` is ≥ 3, else `STANDARD`.
   - **AREA**: `METRO` when the owner's locality region (from `localityRegion(owner)`) is a known region (NSW/VIC/QLD, reusing the existing `REGION_TIMEZONES` table), else `REGIONAL`.

One subtlety worth noting: the initial version threw an NPE for unknown-region owners because `Map.of(...)` (an immutable map) rejects `containsKey(null)`. I fixed it with an explicit null guard before the map lookup, matching how the existing `timezone(owner)` method handles the `null` region case.

All tests pass (`BUILD SUCCESS`, Tests run: 2, Failures: 0), covering both the known-region (`STANDARD_METRO`) and unknown-region (`STANDARD_REGIONAL`) cases.
